parsed.main_gap: Pigeonhole in Section 5 is off: 2^{n+1}-2 proper subset sums give only a gap bound 1/(2^{n+1}-3), not d=1/(2^{n+1}-1). Repairable by including the empty and full subsets.

errors.description: Section 5, eq. (11): with only nonempty proper subsets there are 2^{n+1}-2 values and 2^{n+1}-3 gaps summing to <1, yielding min gap <1/(2^{n+1}-3) > d. The claimed bound d is not derived and is false in general (e.g. n=1, lengths 0.1, 0.9 give gap 0.8). Fix: include S=∅ and S=full (2^{n+1} values, gaps summing to 1), which the later 'one of A,B empty' case already handles.
errors.quote:
They lie in $(0,1)$, so their $2^{n+1}-3$ consecutive gaps sum to less than 1. When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most
\[
\frac1{2^{n+1}-1}=d. \tag{11}
\]

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) with correct greedy-value lemma, correct pairing/discrepancy lemma, a clean tree-component powers-of-two lower bound, and a valid common-refinement cut count. Only the pigeonhole constant is misstated; everything else checks out.
